USMLE-style practice · Pharmacology

Constipation after frequent heartburn treatment

Choose the single best answer, then reveal the explanation.

A 61-year-old woman reports new hard stools after using an aluminum hydroxide antacid several times daily for two weeks. She has no vomiting, distension, weight loss, or change in her other medicines. Which ingredient is most likely responsible for this bowel effect?

  1. Lactulose
  2. Sorbitol
  3. Aluminum hydroxide
  4. Magnesium hydroxide
  5. Polyethylene glycol
Reveal answer and explanation
Correct answer

Aluminum hydroxide

Aluminum hydroxide commonly causes constipation; magnesium salts tend toward the opposite effect.

Understanding the options

Aluminum hydroxide
The temporal relationship fits the constipating effect of aluminum.
Magnesium hydroxide
At usual antacid doses, magnesium tends to cause loose stools.
Polyethylene glycol
Polyethylene glycol is an osmotic laxative.
Lactulose
Lactulose generally draws water into the bowel.
Sorbitol
Sorbitol can cause osmotic diarrhea rather than constipation.
